user.title: OSC Server Setup
user.description: Configure a UDP port for receiving OSC (Open Sound Control) messages. Messages will be routed to Home Assistant entities automatically based on their address.

data_description.port: UDP port to listen on (default: 8000). Make sure this port is not blocked by your firewall.
data_description.debounce_ms: How long to wait (ms) after the last message before acting. Set to 0 to fire every packet immediately. 80–200 ms is recommended for faders and sliders.
data_description.filter_rules:
Optional — one rule per line.

• Start a line with  -  to block an address pattern, e.g.  -/light/*
• Start a line with  +  to explicitly allow a pattern, e.g.  +/light/kitchen
• Lines beginning with # are comments.

Once any + rule is added, only matching addresses are allowed (whitelist mode). Without + rules, everything is allowed except blocked patterns.

error.invalid_filter_rule: Every rule line must start with + (allow) or - (block), or be a comment starting with #.
error.cannot_connect: Could not start the OSC server on that port. The port may already be in use.

abort.already_configured: An OSC server is already configured on that port.

init.title: OSC Server Options
init.description: Changes take effect immediately after saving. The server will restart if the port is changed.

data_description.debounce_ms: Throttle delay in ms. Rapid messages for the same address are collapsed — only the last value is sent to HA once the stream goes quiet. 0 = no throttling.
data_description.filter_rules:
One rule per line.

• -/light/*           → block all lights
• +/light/kitchen     → allow kitchen light (overrides a block)
• -/media_player/*    → block all media players

If any + rule exists, only matching addresses are allowed (whitelist mode).
Lines starting with # are ignored.

error.invalid_filter_rule: Every rule line must start with + (allow) or - (block), or be a comment starting with #.
